newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-AVALANCHE EXTEND UNBEATEN STREAK TO 10 GAMES.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-AVALANCHE EXTEND UNBEATEN STREAK TO 10 GAMES.

text.p: The NHL defending champion Colorado Avalanche extended their unbeaten streak to 10 games on Monday by not worrying about perfection.
Joe Sakic scored twice and Rene Corbet, Aaron Miller and Peter Forsberg each had a goal and an assist as the Avalanche got five unanswered goals to beat the New York Islanders 6-2.
"This was as good as any time we played last year," said Sakic, whose two goals gave him a league-leading 29 points. Forsberg is second in the league with 26.

Eric LaCroix had the other tally and Valeri Kamensky set up three goals for the Avalanche, who won their fourth straight to improve to 8-0-2 in their last 10 games. The franchise record unbeaten streak is 11, set by the Quebec Nordiques from March 10-31, 1981.
"We played well in spots tonight," Colorado coach Marc Crawford said. "We want guys to keep up the good habits.
"Sometimes we try to make the perfect pass. Tonight we had success when we just drove to the net. I'm pleased with the way we came back. We were not perfect, but I'm pleased with the way we played."
Patrick Roy made 32 saves and is 7-0-1 in his last eight starts. He also recorded his league-leading 11th victory.
New York, which got goals from Zigmund Palffy and Derek King, is 0-2-1 in its last three games after going 2-0-1 in its previous three.
"Well that was a game that could be very discouraging," Islanders coach Mike Milbury said.
In Buffalo, Donald Audette's second goal of the game with 59 seconds left in overtime was allowed to stand after replay review and the Sabres beat the Florida Panthers 3-2.
Buffalo's Brian Holzinger broke down the right side on a 2-on-2 and Florida defenceman Paul Laus fell down, allowing Holzinger to skate in uncontested.
Mark Fitzpatrick made a save on Holzinger's shot, but after Richard Smehlik had a swipe at the loose puck, Audette lifted it over the fallen Fitzpatrick for his third goal of the season.
The goal had to be reviewed because the puck entered and left the net so quickly, but after replay, it was allowed to stand.

Radek Dvorak and Ed Jovanovski had goals for the Panthers, who suffered just their second loss of the season (10-2-4). Florida also dropped its first road game of the year, falling to 4-1-3 away from home.
In Montreal, Saku Koivu scored a power-play goal 3:37 of overtime to lift the Canadiens to a 3-2 win over the Edmonton Oilers.

Vladimir Malakhov drove the puck from the blue line and a scramble ensued in front of net. With goalie Curtis Joseph prone on the ice, Koivu picked up the puck in the crease and backhanded it into the right-hand corner.
The Canadiens won at home against the Oilers for the first time since November 1993.
Stephane Richer and Martin Rucinsky had the other Canadien goals. Dean McAmmond and Jason Arnott scored for Edmonton.
Montreal is 2-5-1 in its last eight games. Edmonton fell to 1-4 on its six-game road trip.
In Anaheim, Greg Adams scored the tie-breaking goal late in the second period and Joe Nieuwendyk scored one goal and set up another as the Dallas Stars edged the Mighty Ducks 3-2.
Darryl Sydor had the other goal for the Stars, who improved to 10-1 in their last 11 meetings with the Ducks. Andy Moog made 19 saves for his ninth victory of the season.
Paul Kariya and Alex Hicks tallied for Anaheim, which is an NHL-worst 3-11-3.
In New York, Markus Naslund scored on a stellar individual effort to snap a tie 4:56 into the third period and Kirk McLean made 34 saves to give the Vancouver Canucks a 3-2 victory over the Rangers.

With the game tied 2-2, Naslund skated into the New York zone down the left side. He moved through the faceoff circle and beat defenceman Alexander Karpovtsev before whipping a backhander between the pads of goaltender Mike Richter.

The Rangers pulled Richter for an extra attacker with 30 seconds remaining and had pressure in the Vancouver zone but couldn't beat McLean, who stopped a three-shot flurry with 20 seconds left. He also made a save on Mark Messier with 11 seconds to play.

Mike Sillinger and Bret Hedican also scored for Vancouver, which snapped a seven-game regular-season winless streak in New York (0-6-1) dating to February 1988. The Canucks won twice at Madison Square Garden during the 1994 Stanley Cup Finals.
Wayne Gretzky and Brian Leetch scored for the Rangers, 0-3-1 in their last four games after a four-game unbeaten streak.
